content:
You plan to visit 7 European cities for 16 days in total. You only take direct flights to commute between cities. You would like to visit Oslo for 2 days. You would like to meet your friends at Oslo between day 3 and day 4 to tour together. You want to spend 3 days in Stuttgart. You would like to visit Venice for 4 days. You plan to stay in Split for 4 days. You plan to stay in Barcelona for 3 days. From day 1 to day 3, there is a annual show you want to attend in Barcelona. You would like to visit Brussels for 3 days. You want to meet a friend in Brussels between day 9 and day 11. You would like to visit Copenhagen for 3 days.

Here are the cities that have direct flights:
Venice and Stuttgart, Oslo and Brussels, Split and Copenhagen, Barcelona and Copenhagen, Barcelona and Venice, Brussels and Venice, Barcelona and Stuttgart, Copenhagen and Brussels, Oslo and Split, Oslo and Venice, Barcelona and Split, Oslo and Copenhagen, Barcelona and Oslo, Copenhagen and Stuttgart, Split and Stuttgart, Copenhagen and Venice, Barcelona and Brussels.

Find a trip plan of visiting the cities for 16 days by taking direct flights to commute between them.

Please output the trip plan in the following JSON format:
{"itinerary": [{"day_range": "Day X-Y", "place": "<CITY>"}]}. Include all city visits with their day ranges. Do not include separate flight entries in the JSON output.

IMPORTANT: When you fly from city A to city B on day X, that day counts for BOTH cities. For example:
- If you stay in Venice from Day 1-3 and fly to Vienna on Day 3, then:
  - Venice: Day 1-3 (3 days)
  - Vienna: Day 3-6 (4 days, including the flight day)
- The flight day (Day 3) is counted for both Venice and Vienna.
- Do NOT create separate flight entries in the JSON.

One valid solution is to start in Barcelona (to catch the show during Days 1–3), then fly early to Oslo so that you’re there on Day 3–4 (meeting your Oslo friends), and then visit Split, Stuttgart, Copenhagen, Brussels (so you can meet your Brussels friend on Day 11), and finally end in Venice. One such itinerary (using only direct flights from the list) is as follows:

• Barcelona (3 days: Day 1–3; also hosting the annual show)  
• Oslo (2 days: Day 3–4; so you’re in Oslo on Day 3–4 for your meetup)  
• Split (4 days: Day 4–7)  
• Stuttgart (3 days: Day 7–9)  
• Copenhagen (3 days: Day 9–11)  
• Brussels (3 days: Day 11–13; you can meet your Brussels friend on Day 11, which is within the “between Day 9 and Day 11” window)  
• Venice (4 days: Day 13–16)

How the overlaps work (remember that when you change cities on a flight day that day is counted for both cities):  
– Your Barcelona visit is Day 1–3. On Day 3 you fly to Oslo so that Day 3 counts for both Barcelona and Oslo.  
– Similarly, you depart Oslo on Day 4 (which counts again for both), and so on.  
When you add up the “city days” (3+2+4+3+3+3+4 = 22) but note that there are 6 overlaps (one per flight), the 22 “city days” become 22 – 6 = 16 unique days.

This itinerary also respects the direct‐flight rules:
• Barcelona → Oslo (direct: “Barcelona and Oslo”)  
• Oslo → Split (direct: “Oslo and Split”)  
• Split → Stuttgart (direct: “Split and Stuttgart”)  
• Stuttgart → Copenhagen (direct: “Copenhagen and Stuttgart”)  
• Copenhagen → Brussels (direct: “Copenhagen and Brussels”)  
• Brussels → Venice (direct: “Brussels and Venice”)

Below is the JSON output in the required format.

{
  "itinerary": [
    { "day_range": "Day 1-3", "place": "Barcelona" },
    { "day_range": "Day 3-4", "place": "Oslo" },
    { "day_range": "Day 4-7", "place": "Split" },
    { "day_range": "Day 7-9", "place": "Stuttgart" },
    { "day_range": "Day 9-11", "place": "Copenhagen" },
    { "day_range": "Day 11-13", "place": "Brussels" },
    { "day_range": "Day 13-16", "place": "Venice" }
  ]
}

This plan meets all your requirements while using only direct flights.
